name: Door Sensor
description: A wireless, battery-powered door sensor that reports when the door opens or closes.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor.

steps.text: Remove the sensor's cover.
Install the battery.
Mount the sensor on the door frame.
Mount the magnet on the door, next to the sensor and lined up with it.
Test by opening and closing the door.

notes: The sensor reads closed while the magnet is next to it and open when the magnet moves away.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor's setup.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.

notes: Then turn the responder on (or set it to any state) and press and hold its SET button for 3 seconds; the sensor's LED turns solid green. By default the sensor turns responders on when it opens and off when it closes.
When adding it to a Hub, press and hold the SET button until the LED blinks and then tap the SET button (the LED double-blinks).
The sensor is a controller only.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor's setup.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Tap the SET button.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: While the device is still awake, have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds to finish.

notes: Put the device in linking mode before the Hub starts ALL-Linking. This links the device to the Hub as a controller, with the Hub as the responder, so the Hub receives the device's reports; the Hub makes no link to the device.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's multi-linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, set it to the scene state and press and hold its SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds to finish.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor's setup.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button again for 3 seconds.

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds; the sensor's LED stops blinking and turns solid.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor's setup.

steps.text: While the sensor is awake, send the Stay Awake command (extended, cmd1 0x2E, cmd2 0x00, data 2 0x04, data 3 the number of seconds to stay awake).

notes: The sensor sleeps quickly to save battery and must be awake to send or receive messages; 0xF0 seconds is about 4 minutes, and the maximum is 0xFF.
How to wake the sensor before sending the command isn't known.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor's setup.

steps.text: Unlink any responders from the sensor.
Gently remove the sensor's case with a small screwdriver.
Remove the battery.
Wait at least 15 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button while reinstalling the battery.
Release the SET button when the status LED turns on.
steps.expect: LED stays on about 4 seconds, then turns off

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor's setup.

steps.text: Remove the sensor as a controller from each of its responders.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor's setup.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button again for 3 seconds.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder, for group 0.
steps.expect: The device deletes its link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: If the LED is still blinking, tap the SET button until it stops.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's unlinking steps and the standard Insteon command Start ALL-Linking; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Its heartbeat's cmd1 is 0x11 while it's open and 0x13 while it's closed.
The alias MyLife Door Sensor is inferred: the name it was sold under in a kit; no document gives it.

verification.note: Read from its device category: it shares category 0x10 with the Open/Close Sensor 2843, and its commands, groups and setup are read from that sensor. The HouseLinc device catalog lists subcategory 0x09 as the Door Sensor 2843-232; no other document gives its model number, and none describes the sensor itself.
